newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares closed higher on Friday, reversing an earlier decline on the back of Wall Street's Thursday fall and moving ahead as bonds climbed following remarks from Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing.

Dealers said much of the market's gain today was powered by AEX heavyweight Philips which surged another 3.90 guilders for a two-day gain of 5.60 to 62.20. "The market loved the tough restructuring talk from Philips yesterday," said one.
The AEX closed 5.02 points up at 590.18, back from an early low of 581.46. "It's a bit of a surprise, but the main thing is Philips and we think that can't go on rising," a dealer said.

Dealers said Issing's comments that "under existing circumstances", there could be no rate cut in Germany were not on the face of it bullish but they were heartened that he had not ruled out rate cuts forever as he appeared to have done on German television on Wednesday.
"The bond market went up on what Issing said today and of course that helped shares but we're a bit worried he only seemed to be unpicking what he said the other day," a dealer said.
Dealers speculated that the Philips rise could be topping out. "A lot of this gain is because people who shorted Philips before results yesterday are getting squeezed," a dealer said.
Philips shares on Thursday dropped soon after it unveiled a 77 percent plunge in third quarter net from normal operations to 123 million guilders, prompting widespread short positions.

But comments soon after the results from new chairman Cor Boonstra about an aggressive restructuring brought widescale buying. Turnover on Friday in Philips shares was 11 million -- way above the more normal two million volume.

"We've got a feeling this can't go on for much longer. I can't see any reason why anyone would buy the share at 63 or 64 guilders just because they're restructuring, there's got to be a bit more in the shares than just that," said a dealer.
Unilever stood out with a 3.10 guilder loss to 259.20 with operators taking yesterday's first quarter figures from U.S. group Procter and Gamble as a signal to take profits.

"The (Unilever) shares have had a good run recently on the possibility of a refocusing of the group and people thought the slightly disappointing figures from Procter was a good time for some profit-taking," said a dealer.
Royal Dutch dipped 2.40 guilders to 287.60, ignoring the strong dollar in favour of profit-taking on its own oil-price-related run up recently. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
